title: Surge Sentinel: adaptive 429/timeout/error guardrails and circuit-breaker matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When regional surge or GPU contention occurs we observe a mix of 429s, timeouts, and inflated error rates that lead to client disruptions. Current fallback behavior is ad-hoc and does not differentiate by error signal type or customer tier, leading to noisy failovers and increased cost.

Goal: Implement an adaptive "Surge Sentinel" layer in the routing plane that triggers automatic mitigations (tier-aware rerouting, rate-limit backoff, and controlled circuit trips) based on fused signals: 429 rate, request latency p95/p99 timeouts, and business error-rate. The system should: (1) be configurable per-region and per-tier, (2) support hysteresis and cooldown windows, (3) expose safe rollout flags and metrics, and (4) provide clear observability and a manual override.

Design summary:
- Signal fusion: compute a 1m and 5m weighted score from three normalized signals: 429-rate, timeout-rate, and application error-rate.
- Threshold matrix: use a three-dimensional matrix keyed by region x tier (hosted/dedicated/private) x model-variant to select actions. Actions include: soft-throttle (dynamic rate reduction), prefer-fallback-variant (lower-capacity cheaper model), degrade-to-queued (synchronous -> async), and hard-circuit (reject).
- Circuit behavior: circuits have states CLOSED -> SOFT-OPEN -> OPEN -> PROBATION with configurable tripping thresholds and exponential backoff. SOFT-OPEN triggers non-disruptive mitigations; OPEN triggers immediate failover to fallback variants.
- Hysteresis & cooldown: require sustained breach for 3 consecutive windows by default; cooldown windows scale with severity.
- Tier-awareness: enterprise/dedicated routes have higher tripping thresholds and longer probation to avoid noisy trips for high-SLA customers.
- Telemetry: emit per-route sentinel_score, reason_codes (429,TO,ERR), action_taken, and circuit_state. Sidecar to push events to tracing and the Redwood Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Config-driven matrix can be updated without code deploy; UI/console and API endpoints exist for overrides.
- End-to-end tests that simulate 429/timeouts verify correct action sequences and safe rollback.
- Dashboards show sentinel score, action distribution, and customer-impacting rejects; alerts fire when false-positive rate > 3% or sensitive customers are impacted.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout starting in us-west-2 for non-critical tiers, alpha for internal customers, then staged expansion to other regions and dedicated pools. Canary includes metric checks: decrease in p99 tail tokens served, no increase in end-user latency >2%, and <1% increase in overall cost.

Artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SurgeSentinel; infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1482; runtime PR (circuit state machine): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2693; dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd/surge-sentinel

Notes: This ticket focuses on the routing policy and state machine; downstream work will add automatic model-variant quantization suggestions in Optimize.
